# Bench

Version: 0.0.1

A long seat for several people, typically outdoors in a park, square, street or along a path, available for use by the general public. Extends the Smart Data Models PointOfInterest. Boolean properties follow a tri-state convention: omitted means unknown, false means known to be absent.

## Properties

- `address[object]`: The mailing address. Model: [https://schema.org/address](https://schema.org/address)
- `alternateName[string]`: An alternative name for this item
- `annotations[array]`: Annotations about the item. Model: [https://schema.org/Text](https://schema.org/Text)

- `armrest[boolean]`: Whether the bench has armrests, at the ends or between seats. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM armrest Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `backrest[boolean]`: Whether the bench has a backrest. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM backrest Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `checkDate[string]`: Date the bench was last verified to exist and match its description on the ground. Source: OSM check_date, survey:date Model: [https://schema.org/Date](https://schema.org/Date)
- `color[string]`: The color of the product. Model: [https://schema.org/color](https://schema.org/color)

- `covered[boolean]`: Whether the bench is under a roof or shelter. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM covered Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `dataProvider[string]`: A sequence of characters identifying the provider of the harmonised data entity
- `dateCreated[string]`: Entity creation timestamp. This will usually be allocated by the storage platform

- `description[string]`: A description of this item

- `hostileArchitecture[array]`: Design features that discourage lying or lingering on the bench. Enum:'slanted, separatedSeats, spikes, other'. Source: OSM hostile_architecture Model: [https://schema.org/Text](https://schema.org/Text)
- `id[*]`: Unique identifier of the entity
- `image[string]`: An image of the item. Model: [https://schema.org/URL](https://schema.org/URL)
- `inscription[string]`: Text engraved on or attached to the bench, such as a memorial plaque. Source: OSM inscription Model: [https://schema.org/Text](https://schema.org/Text)
- `level[number]`: Floor level where the bench is located, 0 being ground level. Only relevant indoors or in multi-level structures. Source: OSM level Model: [https://schema.org/Number](https://schema.org/Number)
- `lit[boolean]`: Whether the bench is lit at night. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM lit Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `location[*]`: Geojson reference to the item. It can be Point, LineString, Polygon, MultiPoint, MultiLineString or MultiPolygon
- `lyingDown[boolean]`: Whether the bench is suitable for lying down on. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM lying_down Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `material[string]`: Main material of the seat. Enum:'wood, metal, steel, concrete, stone, granite, plastic'. Source: OSM material Model: [https://schema.org/Text](https://schema.org/Text)
- `memorial[boolean]`: Whether the bench is a memorial bench, dedicated to a person or event. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM memorial=bench Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `name[string]`: The name of this item
- `owner[array]`: A List containing a JSON encoded sequence of characters referencing the unique Ids of the owner(s)
- `seats[integer]`: Number of people who can sit on the bench at the same time. Source: OSM seats Model: [https://schema.org/Integer](https://schema.org/Integer)
- `seatsSeparated[boolean]`: Whether the seats are separated from each other, e.g. by armrests or dividers, so the bench can't be lain on. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM seats:separated Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `seeAlso[*]`: list of uri pointing to additional resources about the item
- `source[string]`: A sequence of characters giving the original source of the entity data as a URL. Recommended to be the fully qualified domain name of the source provider, or the URL to the source object
- `twoSided[boolean]`: Whether people can sit on both sides of the bench. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM two_sided Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)
- `type[string]`: NGSI Entity type. It has to be Bench
- `wasteBasket[boolean]`: Whether a waste basket is attached to or right next to the bench. Omitted means unknown; false means known to be absent. Source: OSM bin Model: [https://schema.org/Boolean](https://schema.org/Boolean)

## Required properties

- `id`
- `location`
- `type`

Describes a public bench for city services, accessibility and wayfinding apps (e.g. routes with places to rest) and maintenance. Attributes follow OpenStreetMap amenity=bench tagging, https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:amenity%3Dbench, and each property's schema description names its OSM key, "Source: ...". The attribute set was checked against an Overpass export of 2,265 benches in Aarhus (2026-09-30). Share of benches carrying each key, backrest 87%, material 48% (wood 990, concrete 44, metal 17, plastic 14, granite 9, stone 8, steel 1), armrest 31%, check_date or survey:date 5%, seats 4%, direction 4%, colour 1%, lying_down 20, two_sided 14, seats:separated 4, bin 2, lit 1, level 1, hostile_architecture 1 (slanted). OSM keys covered and inscription didn't appear in the export but are standard bench tags and are included.

Smart Data Models has no bench model; its generic OSMAmenity lists bench as an amenityType but has no bench attributes. This entity type therefore extends https://smart-data-models.github.io/dataModel.PointOfInterest/PointOfInterest/schema.json, reusing its common definitions GSMA-Commons, Location-Commons and contactPoint (Contact-Commons, used for fault reporting), plus PhysicalObject-Commons for color (OSM colour) and image (e.g. a Panoramax photo URL, OSM panoramax). Unlike PointOfInterest, name is not required, since benches rarely have one (3 of 2,265 in the export). Boolean properties are tri-state, omitted means unknown and false means known to be absent. Publishers should omit rather than default to false. When importing from OSM, use source for the element URL (e.g. https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/888668859) and dataProvider for attribution; OSM data is licensed under ODbL. Benches mapped as ways are exported by Overpass as their centre point, which is what location holds.

OSM keys deliberately not mapped, amenity (implied by the entity type), note (free text for mappers; use description, or inscription for engravings), access (3 benches, all yes; benches in this model are public), not:* keys (mapper hints), panoramax (map to image as a URL), and tourism=artwork with artwork_type and artist_name (1 bench; an artwork bench is better also published as an artwork entity). Open points, (a) the OSM wiki page couldn't be fetched when this model was written, so the key list and value sets (material, hostile_architecture) should be re-checked against it, (b) OSM direction also allows cardinal values (N, NE, …), which publishers must convert to degrees, (c) material values beyond the listed ones are dropped rather than mapped, (d) a companion BenchObserved entity for condition and faults is not included.
